title: The Volcano Boom Heard 10,000 km Away
description:
Unreal but true: a new real event every day at 5:48 pm (Riyadh).

On January 15, 2022, the underwater volcano Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai in Tonga erupted in the most powerful explosion recorded by modern instruments. Its booms were heard across Alaska, more than 10,000 km (6,200 miles) away. The pressure wave it sent through the atmosphere kept circling the planet for days: four times in one direction and three times in the other.

The eruption and its tsunami killed several people in Tonga and as far away as Peru, and covered much of Tonga in ash.

The map is drawn so every circle around the volcano is a true distance; the wave on screen is sped up, not real time.

Sources: Live Science, "Tonga volcano eruption sent atmospheric waves around Earth" (2022); University of Liverpool, "Tonga eruption as powerful as Krakatoa" (study in Science, May 2022). Distances are great-circle distances from the volcano. Map: Natural Earth.
Animation drawn in code; narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs).

Did you guess right? Would you have heard it where you live?
